metadata.title: Function Composition: g then f
metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.objective: Show g(x) then f(g(x)) as a two-stage machine.
expectedUnderstanding: the intermediate value is g(x) and the final value is f(g(x))
stage order changes the result for these functions
f is applied to g's output, not multiplied by it

checkpoints.title: The input enters stage g
checkpoints.body: The token is the input x, set with the slider. It reaches g first, so g is evaluated before f is applied. A composition runs right to left: the function nearest x acts first.

checkpoints.title: Inside g: the intermediate value
checkpoints.body: At this moment only g has been applied. The left bar is g(x) = x^2 - 1, which is not the final answer. With x = 1.5 it is 1.25; with x = 0 it is -1.

checkpoints.title: Inside f: g's output is the input
checkpoints.body: f receives g(x), not x. The rule is f(u) = u/2 + 1 with u = g(x), so at x = 1.5 the right bar is f(1.25) = 1.625. The right bar is shorter than the left because f halves its input.

checkpoints.title: Order matters
checkpoints.body: Use x = 2 in both orders: f(g(2)) = f(3) = 2.5, but g(f(2)) = g(2) = 3. The two results differ, so swapping the stages changes the answer. Composition is also not multiplication: f(3) is 2.5, not 1.5 times 3.

checkpoints.title: A negative intermediate is fine
checkpoints.body: Set x = 0: g(0) = -1, so the left bar points below the baseline, and f(-1) = 0.5 still has a value. The intermediate output does not have to be positive for the composition to work.

narration.text: The token is the input x; it flows through g first, then f.
Inside g the value is the intermediate g(x), not the answer.
f is applied to g's output, so the right bar is f(g(x)).
Swapping the two stages changes the result.

fallback.text: A token passes through stage g (square the input, subtract 1) and then stage f (halve, add 1). The lower bars show the intermediate g(x) and the final f(g(x)) on a shared zero line. For example x = 1.5 gives g = 1.25 then f = 1.625, while x = 0 gives g = -1 then f = 0.5.

accessibility.alt: A token passing through two labelled boxes, g then f, with two vertical bars below showing the intermediate value g(x) and the final value f(g(x)) on a shared baseline.
